title: reduce-streaming-token-latency-kernel-scheduling-kv-cache-batching-backpressure
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Streaming token generation latency is a critical SLO for interactive applications. Customers reported elevated tail latency when streams compete with batch workloads and when KV cache warm paths miss under preemption. This PR combines several coordinated runtime changes to reduce per-token latency in the common streaming path: 1) low-latency kernel scheduling: introduce a fast-path scheduler that prioritizes short, latency-sensitive token loops and avoids larger kernel launches that increase tail time; 2) KV cache warm-path improvements: opportunistically populate per-request KV cache before first token emission and add a non-blocking read path for cold keys; 3) continuous batching heuristics: adjust batch formation timeout and batch size caps when a request is marked streaming to prefer smaller, earlier batches; 4) backpressure and flush cadence: refine backpressure signals and add an adaptive flush cadence that triggers earlier flushes on low-throughput interactive sessions, and a forced flush after a configurable idle threshold to prevent stalls. Summary of changes: - runtime/kernel_scheduler.rs: add LowLatencyScheduler and heuristics to avoid expensive kernel preemption for streaming requests. - runtime/kv_cache.rs: add async warm-path hooks and optimize lock granularity for cache reads. - runtime/batching.rs: add streaming-aware BatchHints and dynamic timeout adjustment. - runtime/streaming.rs: integrate new flush cadence and backpressure signals into the token loop. - tests/perf/stream_latency.py: new perf harness for 99p/median token latency under mixed workloads. - docs/release_notes/52134.md: brief user-facing note. Commits: - "Introduce LowLatencyScheduler and streaming hints" - "KV cache warm-path + lock optimization" - "Continuous batching: streaming-aware timeouts" - "Adaptive flush cadence and backpressure tuning" Testing and validation: - Unit tests added for scheduler decision logic and KV cache non-blocking path. - Perf harness run against a mixed workload (50% streaming, 50% batch) across p3/4-like machines. Results show median per-token latency reduction of ~18% and 99th percentile reduction of ~28% for streaming requests compared to baseline. - Canary rollout on Dedicated with staged traffic to validate no regression for batch-heavy customers. Backwards compatibility: no API changes; opt-in tunables exposed via runtime config flags. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2217) - [x] Linear/Implementation tracked (ENG-2260, ENG-2301) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Perf results attached - [x] Docs updated - [x] SRE review requested Notes: The scheduler change adds a small heuristic weight to request metadata (is_streaming, expected_output_len). The heuristic is conservative and tunable via runtime flags; default behavior preserves throughput for pure-batch runs. Release risk classified as medium; rollout includes a staged canary and automated rollback if token latency regressions exceed threshold.

release_notes: Reduce streaming token latency by ~18% median and ~28% 99th percentile in mixed workloads.
Introduces a low-latency scheduler fast-path for streaming requests (tunable).
KV cache warm-path and lock optimizations reduce cold-key read latency.
Streaming-aware batching heuristics and adaptive flush cadence to avoid stalls on interactive sessions.
benchmark_summary: Mixed workflow (50% streaming / 50% batch) on p3-style nodes: median per-token latency reduced from 42ms to 34.4ms (-18%), 99th percentile reduced from 210ms to 151ms (-28%). End-to-end generation latency for 32-token responses improved by ~12% under typical load.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover scheduler decision paths and KV cache non-blocking reads. Perf harness run 1000 streams in parallel with 10k total requests; results captured in benchmarks/streaming_mixed_workload.yaml. Canary deployed to 5% traffic for 24h with automated alerts. No rolling restarts required for config changes.
